newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Late Nobel laureate will be honoured - committee.
newsitem.headline: Late Nobel laureate will be honoured - committee.

text.p: Canadian-born economist William Vickrey, who died on Friday three days after learning he had won a Nobel Prize, will still be honoured, Swedish Nobel officials said on Saturday.

One of his family members would probably be asked to receive his half share of the $1.12 million 1996 economics prize in his honour at the award ceremony hosted by the Swedish Nobel Committee in Stockholm on December 10, the head of the committee, Jorgen Weibull, told reporters.

Michael Sohlman, managing director of the Nobel Foundation which awards the prizes, told the Dagens Nyheter newspaper that Vickrey's death would in no way affect the Nobel Committee's decision and that Vickery would remain the official winner of the economics prize along with James Mirrlees.
A prize winner must be alive when the decision is announced, said Stig Ramel, the Nobel Foundation's former head.
"A person must be alive at the time of the announcement of the winner, but after a decision has been made a person becomes a laureate with the announcement," Ramel told the newspaper.

Vickrey, who was 82, died early on Friday after suffering a heart attack at the wheel of his car while driving from New York to Boston, Massachusetts, for a conference of a group he founded, TRED (Taxation, Resources, Economics and Development). He had worked at Columbia University in New York for 60 years.
Vickrey and British economist James Mirrlees, 60, shared the prize for their separate contributions "to the economic theory of incentives under asymmetric information".
The research of both men, who had never met, focused on how organisations could make competent decisions based on incomplete -- or asymmetric -- information.
